source_text:
Ὑμεῖς οὖν οἱ τὴν καταβολὴν τῆς στάσεως ποιήσαντες ὑποτάγητε τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις καὶ παιδεύθητε εἰς μετάνοιαν, κάμψαντες τὰ γόνατα τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν.
μάθετε ὑποτάσσεσθαι, ἀποθέμενοι τὴν ἀλαζόνα καὶ ὑπερήφανον τῆς γλώσσης ὑμῶν αὐθάδειαν: ἄμεινον γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῖν, ἐν τῷ ποιμνίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μικροὺς καὶ ἐλλογίμους εὑρεθῆναι, ἢ καθ̓ ὑπεροχὴν δοκοῦντας ἐκριφῆναι ἐκ τῆς ἐλπίδος αὐτοῦ.
οὕτως γὰρ λέγει ἡ πανάρετος σοφία: Ἰδού, προήσομαι ὑμῖν ἐμῆς πνοῆς ῥῆσιν, διδάξω δὲ ὑμᾶς τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον.
ἐπειδὴ ἐκάλουν καὶ οὐχ ὑπηκούσατε, καὶ ἐξέτεινον λόγους καὶ οὐ προσείχετε, ἀλλὰ ἀκύρους ἐποιεῖτε τὰς ἐμὰς βουλάς, τοῖς δὲ ἐμοῖς ἐλέγχοις ἠπειθήσατε: τοιγαροῦν κἀγὼ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ ἀπωλείᾳ ἐπιγελάσομαι, καταχαροῦμαι δὲ ἡνίκα ἂν ἔρχηται ὑμῖν ὄλεθρος καὶ ὡς ἂν ἀφίκηται ὑμῖν ἄφνω θόρυβος, ἡ δὲ καταστροφὴ ὁμοία καταιγίδι παρῇ, ἢ ὅταν ἔρχηται ὑμῖν θλίψις καὶ πολιορκία.
ἔσται γὰρ ὅταν ἐπικαλέσησθέ με, ἐγὼ δὲ οὐκ εἰσακούσομαι ὑμῶν: ζητήσουσίν με κακοί, καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσουσιν. ἐμίσησαν γὰρ σοφίαν, τὸν δὲ φόβον τοῦ κυρίου οὐ προείλαντο, οὐδὲ ἤθελον ἐμαῖς προσέχειν βουλαῖς, ἐμυκτήριζον δὲ ἐμοὺς ἐλέγχους.
τοιγαροῦν ἔδονται τῆς ἑαυτῶν ὁδοῦ τοὺς καρπούς, καὶ τῆς ἑαυτῶν ἀσεβείας πλησθήσονται:
ἀνθ̓ ὦν γὰρ ἠδίκουν νηπίους φονευθήσονται, καὶ ἐξετασμὸς ἀσεβεῖς ὀλεῖ: ὁ δὲ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι πεποιθὼς καὶ ἡσυχάσει ἀφόβως ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ.
thought_title: Warning to the Faction-Makers: Submit or Perish
orientation: The Roman church, having just quoted Job on God's fatherly discipline, now turns directly to the Corinthians who started the faction and commands them to submit to the elders and repent, quoting Wisdom's warning to the disobedient.
pass_a_gloss: You therefore, the [ones] who made the foundation of the faction, submit to the elders and be disciplined into repentance, having bent the knees of your heart. Learn to submit, having put off the boastful and arrogant self-will of your tongue; for [it is] better for you, in the flock of Christ, to be found small and reputable, than, seeming [great] according to preeminence, to be cast out from his hope. For thus says the all-virtuous Wisdom: Behold, I will pour forth to you a saying of my breath, and I will teach you my word. Since I was calling and you did not obey, and I was stretching out words and you did not attend, but you were making my counsels void, and to my reproofs you were disobedient: therefore I also will laugh at your destruction, and I will rejoice when ruin comes to you and when suddenly tumult arrives to you, and the overthrow like a storm is present, or when affliction and siege comes to you. For it will be [that] when you call upon me, I will not listen to you; evil [ones] will seek me, and will not find [me]. For they hated wisdom, and the fear of the Lord they did not choose, nor did they wish to attend to my counsels, and they were mocking my reproofs. Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way, and of their own impiety they will be filled: for because of what they were doing wrong to infants they will be murdered, and examination will destroy impious [ones]; but the [one] hearing me will dwell in hope, trusting, and will be quiet without fear from all evil.

lemmas.gloss: having put off, having laid aside
I will pour forth, send forth

choices.why: καταβολή means a laying down or founding; 'foundation' keeps the metaphor of the faction as something built, and 'faction' is the fixed glossary term for στάσις.
The passive imperative with εἰς marks the goal of the discipline; 'into repentance' preserves the directional force and the glossary term 'repentance' for μετάνοια.
A literal rendering of the metaphor keeps the bodily image of bending knees applied to the inner person; 'heart' is the standard rendering of καρδία.
rejected: the knees of your inner being

choices.why: μικρός means small or humble in status, and ἐλλόγιμος means counted among the notable or esteemed; the pairing contrasts humility with false preeminence.
ὑπεροχή means preeminence or superiority; δοκοῦντας marks the appearance rather than reality, which is key to the contrast with being found small.
πανάρετος means possessing all virtue; personified Wisdom is the speaker of the following quotation, so the capital W marks the personification.

bible_refs.note: Ἰδού, προήσομαι ὑμῖν ἐμῆς πνοῆς ῥῆσιν, διδάξω δὲ ὑμᾶς τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον... ἐπειδὴ ἐκάλουν καὶ οὐχ ὑπηκούσατε... τοιγαροῦν κἀγὼ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ ἀπωλείᾳ ἐπιγελάσομαι... ζητήσουσίν με κακοί, καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσουσιν... ὁ δὲ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων κατασκηνώσει ἐπ' ἐλπίδι πεποιθὼς

pass_b_english: So then, you who laid the foundation of this faction: submit to the elders, and accept discipline that leads you into repentance. Bend the knees of your heart.

Learn to submit. Put off the boastful and proud self-will of your tongue, because it is better for you to be found small and reputable in the flock of Christ than to appear great through preeminence and be cast out from his hope.
For this is what the all-virtuous Wisdom says: "Look, I will pour out to you the utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word" (Proverbs 1:23).

"Because I called and you would not obey, I stretched out my words and you paid no attention" (Proverbs 1:24). "You made my counsels void and disobeyed my reproofs. So I in turn will laugh at your destruction, and I will gloat when ruin comes upon you, when sudden tumult arrives, when catastrophe overtakes you like a storm, when affliction and siege come upon you."

"Then you will call upon me, but I will not listen to you. Evil people will seek me and will not find me, because they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord" (Proverbs 1:28-29). "They had no wish to attend to my counsels, and they mocked my reproofs."
"Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way, and they will be filled with their own impiety."

"For the wrongs they did to the innocent, they will be slain, and searching judgment will destroy the impious. But the one who listens to me will dwell in hope, trusting, and will be quiet, with no fear of any evil" (Proverbs 1:32-33).

problems.why: καταχαροῦμαι means 'I will exult over, gloat over' (with malicious joy); 'rejoice' loses the negative, mocking sense. 'I will gloat' or 'I will exult'.
problems.ruling: καταχαροῦμαι = gloat/exult over (malicious joy); 'rejoice' loses the mocking sense, misleading readers.

problems.why: ἐξετασμός here means 'inquiry, scrutiny, investigation' leading to judgment; 'examination' suggests a test. 'Scrutiny' or 'inquiry' or 'searching judgment'.
problems.ruling: ἐξετασμός = scrutiny/inquiry bringing judgment; 'examination' misleads readers into thinking of a test, not judgment.

edits.new: searching judgment will destroy the impious

problems.quote: For the wrongs they did to infants, they will be murdered
problems.source_quote: ἀνθ̓ ὦν γὰρ ἠδίκουν νηπίους φονευθήσονται
problems.why: νηπίους means 'innocent/simple ones', not 'infants'; φονευθήσονται is passive 'will be slain/murdered', but 'they will be murdered' changes agency—who murders? The Greek says they will be slain as punishment.
problems.fix: For they wronged the innocent, they will be slain

fixed: The other two reported problems were already addressed in the current English: 'I will rejoice' was changed to 'I will gloat', and 'examination will destroy the impious' was changed to 'searching judgment will destroy the impious'.

problems.why: In this era, bishop/elder/presbyter were often the same office; inconsistent terms confuse the hierarchy.
problems.fix: Add a note explaining the overlapping use of these terms.

problems.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
problems.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.
